objective: Proof and verification. Grid law: a decoupling lemma (large height distances between the split point's regions and a line's regions make the line independent of the split point) and the lemma that independence leaves no crossing knot through handle points; certificates on the grids. Ladder law: Boolean transfer matrices around the prism make the transfer to far lines eventually constant in size and position, reducing every prism to finitely many cases.
status: Proved by PHASE-HALO-20261103-001B-P001: the prism over a 2k-cycle is the cyclic chain of consecutive triples, with Kasteleyn signs constant except at two lines beside the attachment point, and its transfer matrix repeats with period 2 from the second power, so every far line's transfer depends only on its parity on every prism; with the route criterion, an opened Fano handle's halo runs the full opposite face on every prism (computed k = 5 to 40). On grids, far lines have the full transfer (certified exactly) and are independent of the handle; height ranges between ports and lines are 0 on ladders and grow on grids
title: The ladder and grid laws
